messages:
marta: Running into TLS verify failures when talking to our Dedicated inside the customer's VPC. Sync calls (requests) pass with custom CA but Async (httpx) errors out. Anyone seen this?
dave: What's the exact error and how are you configuring the SDK? base_url/proxy etc?
marta: Error is `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: unable to get local issuer certificate`. I'm using sdk.AsyncClient(base_url=\"https://svc.internal\", api_key=...) and I set verify='/etc/pki/tls/certs/custom-ca.pem' on the client init.
emma: Do you mean you call sdk.AsyncClient(verify=...) or you make an httpx.AsyncClient and hand it in?
marta: Tried both: passing verify into sdk constructor, and also building an httpx.AsyncClient(verify='/etc/pki/tls/certs/custom-ca.pem') and wrapping it: sdk.AsyncClient(httpx_client=client). Sync path works either way. Async path still fails.
dave: Could be how our wrapper normalizes kwargs for async. We injected a transport layer for retries/proxy and might be dropping the SSLContext.
emma: Also check the typing stubs in sdk/_client.py. I remember we typed `verify: Optional[bool]` for AsyncClient to mirror requests historically. If code downstream assumes bool it may call `bool(verify)` somewhere.
marta: I grepped: in async wrapper we do `_build_transport(verify=verify)` and inside that function we do `if not verify: return default_transport` which treats a path string as truthy fine, but later we call `ssl.create_default_context()` only when verify is True (bool), not when it's a str. So path gets ignored. oof.
dave: Yikes. So two problems: wrong branching for str vs bool, and the typing stub being wrong which will confuse users and linters.
emma: For an immediate repro, you can run a local HTTPS server using Python's http.server with ssl and a CA signed cert and try both clients. For CI test write a small unit that creates an SSLContext from the PEM and asserts the async client's transport has that context.
marta: Workaround that worked for me: create SSLContext manually and pass it in:
```py
import ssl, httpx
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/pki/tls/certs/custom-ca.pem')
async_client = httpx.AsyncClient(verify=ctx)
sdk_client = sdk.AsyncClient(httpx_client=async_client, base_url='https://svc.internal', api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
```
This avoids the SDK path that converts strings to contexts.
dave: Good. Please paste that snippet to the issue. Also note env vars: `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` differ across libs; add a short note in quickstart.
emma: I'll take the issue. Plan: 1) fix conditional to detect `isinstance(verify, (str, bytes, ssl.SSLContext))` and call `ssl.create_default_context(cafile=...)` when verify is path; 2) update type hints to `Union[bool, str, ssl.SSLContext]`; 3) ensure retry middleware doesn't re-create transports without copying ssl context; 4) add regression test using temporary certs.
dave: Also consider exposing an explicit `tls` param on sdk.AsyncClient that is documented, so users don't have to guess whether `verify` will be forwarded.
emma: Good idea for ergonomics; file INF-4201 for feature request.
infra-bot: New issue INF-4187 created and assigned to emma: "python sdk async: ensure custom CA paths produce SSLContext and are preserved through retry transport"
marta: Thanks team. Can we also add a troubleshooting FAQ in Dedicated onboarding about proxies, custom CA, and example sync/async snippets? This bit cost me a half day.
dave: Agreed. I'll add a short blurb to the onboarding checklist and link the SDK PR once merged.
emma: Opening a PR now, will include the test and the docs blurb. ETA EOW.
marta: Lovely. I'll verify on their staging VPC when the patch lands.
